bugs_found.where: lib/wf.py:94 outcomes() cache key (id(df), len, first close, last close, target, stop, cost)
bugs_found.what: The cache can return stale results. Two cases were shown in verify/code_auditor/cache_check.py: (1) changing a DataFrame in place (high += 1000) still returns the old outcomes; (2) after garbage collection, a new DataFrame with different content got the same id() and was given the cached outcomes of the old one.
bugs_found.impact: No effect on any reported number. evaluate.py builds one DataFrame per process and keeps it alive without changing it. Candidates and lookahead_check never pass changed frames to outcomes(). The agents' discovery scripts never assign price columns. Fresh re-runs of locked/evaluate.py give output identical to logs/validation.jsonl (8/8) and logs/holdout.jsonl. An independent bar-by-bar simulator matches wf.backtest trade for trade (entry, exit, pnl) for all 8 candidates, 3 periods and 3 cost modes. The discovery_results.json numbers reproduce from clean processes. This is a latent defect only.

bugs_found.what: The p-value is anti-conservative. It draws each trade independently from a 30-minute bucket pool, so it ignores the correlation between trades on the same day (time_of_day_1 averages about 2.4 trades per day). Its null mean also includes the cost and bracket asymmetry (about -32 pts per trade), so the baseline is easy to beat.
bugs_found.impact: It made validation look better than it was, not worse. For time_of_day_1 on validation the reported p was 0.022. Nulls that keep day clustering give: day-shuffle 0.032, day sign-flip 0.081, day bootstrap P(total<=0) 0.116 (one-sided p from daily t 1.19 is about 0.12). With a clustered p, time_of_day_1 probably fails the pre-registered PROMISSOR bar (p<0.05), the holdout is never opened, and the result is the same 'no edge'. Holdout p goes from 0.24 to between 0.15 and 0.46 depending on the null. Neither changes the verdict.

bugs_found.where: lib/wf.py build()/outcomes() with locked/evaluate.py holdout days (2012-09-20 has 35 bars, ending 09:34)
bugs_found.what: The truncated final day counts as a full holdout day, and its 09:34 bar is treated as the end-of-day forced exit.
bugs_found.impact: Negligible. time_of_day_1 cannot signal before 10:05; its holdout t_daily is 0.128 with either 20 or 19 days. Only volume_flow_1, which was not sent to holdout, would have one truncated trade (-18.8 pts).

summary:
I read wf.py (all 249 lines) and evaluate.py (all 52 lines) line by line and tested each suspicion with scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-codex-teste/6018d537-360c-53a0-852b-fd7bc8336aa9/scratchpad/edge/verify/code_auditor/ (data_check.py, ohlc_check.py, indep_sim.py, history_check.py, cache_check.py, baseline_check.py, fill_sensitivity.py, misc_check.py, plus fresh evaluate.py re-runs in rerun_*.jsonl). I modified nothing under lib, locked, candidates or logs.

**Data**
- 50,000 rows; no duplicate or unsorted timestamps; aft='N' everywhere.
- Every day runs 09:00-17:29 except the last day, 2012-09-20 (35 bars, ends 09:34). A few minutes are missing on 5 days; none fall in the 10:05-10:30 window.
- The OHLC labels are consistent: low <= open,close <= high in 100% of bars, and |open[i+1]-close[i]| averages 1.06 ticks against 5.3 ticks for the bar range.

**Tick estimation**
- The tick is correct on every day, including the 35-bar day: 12.7807 until the June roll, then 12.6564, then 12.5185 from 2012-08-15.
- Every price sits on the tick grid (max deviation 0.004 tick).

**Simulator**
- My independent bar-by-bar simulator reproduces wf.backtest exactly for all 8 candidates in discovery, validation and holdout, under zero, base and stress costs. No off-by-one in entry, exit, triu, stop gaps or end-of-day exits.

**Warm-up and history**
- Discovery results are identical whether computed on the 59-day frame, the 79-day frame or the full 99-day frame with entry_days. Validation and holdout results are identical on the longer frames.
- Results change only on frames with no warm-up at all (for levels_calendar and volume_flow, which use the prior close or 10 days of volume). evaluate.py correctly gives that warm-up.
- entry_days filtering, the busy_until logic and the daily stats denominators are correct.

**Cache**
- The cache defect is real but latent (see bugs). The logs reproduce byte-identically, and the candidate sha256 hashes match PRE_REGISTRO.md.

**Fills**
- The stop-wins-ties rule never fired: there were 0 same-bar target/stop collisions in any period.
- No target exit had a favourable gap that a better fill model would have credited (0 of 22).
- Fill and cost rules cannot rescue the holdout. Under zero cost with touch fills, time_of_day_1 makes +11.1/trade (n=45, t_daily 0.13). Even with an infeasible entry at the signal bar's close and zero cost it makes only +22.7/trade (t 0.28).
- time_of_day_2, the same hypothesis with one entry per day, made -145.7/trade in holdout.

**Discovery inflation**
- No defect inflates discovery. All reported discovery totals reproduce; ml_walkforward's figure is the agent's walk-forward number, and the frozen in-sample version gives 8698.6, n=208.
- Reading each candidate showed no lookahead.
- No discovery script reads beyond load(): there are no all_days, build or read_csv calls in logs/*.
- The discovery numbers are inflated by selection across 21,243 variants, not by a bug.

**Verdict**
- The conclusion holds: nothing in the code or the evaluation causes a false negative, and the only statistical defect (the anti-conservative random_baseline) makes the validation look better than it was.
- Caveat for how it is worded: the out-of-sample tests have low power. The holdout per-trade 95% CI is about [-166, +189]. In a rough day-bootstrap check, the pre-registered holdout test would pass only about 55% of the time even if the true edge equalled the discovery estimate of 125/trade.
- So 'no edge demonstrated; the discovery-sized effect is disfavored (z = -1.26 on holdout alone)' is more accurate than 'edge proven absent'.

bugs_found.what: Stress doubles entry slippage, exit slippage and fees (2/2/1 tick) but leaves the target trade-through at 1 tick instead of 2. I found this by searching over cost definitions: (2,2,1,through=1) reproduces all three reported stress totals exactly (10,633.4 / 4,453.1 / -514.0). This is a definition choice, not a coding error.
bugs_found.impact: With trade-through also doubled, validation stress falls from +4,453 to +941 (n=44) and holdout stress from -514 to -2,027 (n=40). Discovery is unchanged. No decision changes: validation stays 'promising' and holdout still fails. The current stress is a bit lenient, so it favours the candidate rather than hiding an edge.

bugs_found.what: The file ends at 09:34 on 2012-09-20, so that day has only 35 bars and no 10:05-10:29 window. The holdout therefore has 19 tradable days, not 20, and t_daily counts that day as a zero.
bugs_found.impact: Negligible: holdout t_daily is 0.13 whether that day is included or not. Losing one day slightly lowers an already weak test's power. It does not bias the result.

bugs_found.what: The 'random' baseline is a looser null than random direction at the same entry times. My test flips each day's trade directions at random, keeping the entry times: validation p=0.075 (base costs) and 0.19 (zero costs). Validation+holdout together: p=0.078 (base) and 0.26 (zero).
bugs_found.impact: Validation looked more promising than it was. This works against a false negative, not toward one.

summary:
My own loader and bracket simulator, written from the raw CSV and the stated rules without looking at wf.py or evaluate.py, reproduce every reported zero-cost and base-cost number for time_of_day_1 to the decimal in all three periods. The candidate was neither inflated by a bug nor hurt by one, so the conclusion stands. The one weak spot is power: the holdout was too short to rule out a real edge.

What I checked:
- **Data:** 99 days, sorted, no duplicates; every day starts at 09:00. Each day's tick (12.78, then 12.66 from 2012-06-13, then 12.52 from 2012-08-15) changes only between days, at the futures rollovers. All prices sit on that day's tick grid. No bars are missing inside 10:05-10:29.
- **Rule mechanics:** the bracket is set from the slipped fill price. A new signal may fire on the close of the bar where the previous trade exited (the evaluator does the same). Gap-fill handling on stops makes no difference.

Why base beats zero in validation (+4,457 vs +3,500): with re-entries, costs change exit bars and so change where later entries happen. I checked trade by trade (2012-08-08, 08-14, 08-17, 08-22). It is path noise, not a bug.

How fragile the result is:
- Bracket from the raw open instead of the fill, base costs: holdout -570, validation +2,358.
- Re-entry only from the bar after the exit, base costs: holdout -2,007, validation +2,483.

Small, reasonable implementation choices flip the holdout sign, so the out-of-sample number is mostly noise.

Discovery: exact reproduction means no simulator inflation. The inflation is selection: about 2,300 variants in this research line (21,243 in total), and the window and anchor were tuned on the same data.

Adversarial caveat (the strongest case against the negative reading): the test had little power.
- The daily P&L standard deviation is about 850 points out of sample.
- Even if the full discovery edge (233.7 points/day) were real, 19 holdout days would give an expected t of 1.2 and about 33% power at one-sided 5%.
- At half the discovery edge, power is about 15%.
- So 'no edge survived' means 'not shown', not 'shown absent'.

A simpler variant I chose after seeing the out-of-sample data:
- One trade per day: signal at the 10:05 close, enter at the 10:06 open, exit at the 10:35 close.
- It is positive in both validation (t 1.80) and holdout (t 1.90); combined 39 days, t 2.64, Wilcoxon p=0.02.
- But I picked the exit time from 8 horizons after seeing out-of-sample data. Dropping the two best days cuts the per-period t to about 1.0-1.2, and the 500/500 first trade of each day lost money in both out-of-sample periods.
- At most this is a hypothesis for a new forward test. It does not reverse the pre-registered verdict.

Window-shift sensitivity, validation+holdout, zero costs: -10 min: +4,000; -5: +7,000; 0: +4,000; +5: +7,000; +10: -2,001; daily t is between -0.33 and 1.34. The windows overlap heavily, so these are not independent. There is a weak positive sign nearby, but nothing significant.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-codex-teste/6018d537-360c-53a0-852b-fd7bc8336aa9/scratchpad/edge/verify/independent_reimplementation/: sim.py (loader, simulator and rule), sens.py (window shifts) and extra.py (fixed-horizon test, randomization, power).
